title: I Let Legal Advice Start With a Parking Boot I Did Not Earn

parts.text: I found a boot on my Civic at 7:12 a.m. and the office still smelled like lemon mop water. I am twenty-two, delivery driver, late for a route. The note said unpaid visitor parking. I live here. My sticker was on the glass, faded but legal. The manager, Trina, ate a yogurt behind the plexiglass. "System says visitor," she said. I said, "System is wrong." She shrugged. "Pay seventy or wait for appeal, ten business days." I had a refrigerated bag of poke in the back seat. I photographed the sticker, the boot, and the empty visitor log on the podium. My neighbor Hasan came down in slides. "They did my sister last month. Same yogurt." Trina tapped the plexiglass. "No loitering." I paid because poke waits for no appeal. The receipt named a vendor, ClampCo, not the building. I emailed the lease clause about resident stickers. Trina auto-replied she was at a conference. Hasan said the conference was her cousin's barbecue. I checked the resident portal. My sticker status: active. Visitor status: none. Then ClampCo called me, cheerful. "Sir, your vehicle is in our system as a repeat visitor. Third boot pending." I was standing in the lobby. Trina's yogurt paused. The plexiglass had a crack shaped like a lightning bolt. She mouthed, don't take that here. My phone was already on speaker.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: ClampCo is calling me a repeat visitor on speaker while the portal says my sticker is active.

social.video_title: They booted a resident as a visitor — Part 1/2
social.description: Lemon mop water, poke in the back seat, and a yogurt pause behind plexiglass. The vendor already wanted a third boot. Would you have paid the seventy?

parts.text: I said, "This is the property manager's lobby, and my portal says active resident." ClampCo went quiet, then. She said, "Must be a glitch." I asked them to email the glitch. They did, cc'ing a district number she had not wanted. I requested a refund in writing. Ten days later the seventy returned minus a "processing" five dollars. I disputed the five with my bank using the portal screenshot. I won. The third-boot threat vanished. Trina posted a sign: visitors must use codes, residents must not argue with vendors. Hasan taped a sticky note under it: vendors must not argue with leases. It lasted an afternoon. I filed a complaint with the city parking-consumer line because boots on residents with active stickers are a product, not a vibe. An inspector visited. The lemon mop was extra that day. ClampCo lost the contract. The new company actually looks at stickers. Trina still eats yogurt. I still deliver poke. Sometimes the faded sticker peels and I press it back with my thumb, a stupid ritual that means I live here. The plexiglass crack is still there. I consider it a witness. The cheap light over the sink flickered twice like punctuation I did not ask for.
